packs.title: Art, Gardens and River
packs.promise: Explore Richmond through separate art, garden, river and memory outings.

q.s: Compare how two credited artworks frame a subject.
st: Choose two credited works in open permanent galleries and record their makers.
Note one visible framing, material or color choice in each.
Write an original comparison that separates observation from any guess about the makers' intentions.

q.s: Turn a museum demonstration into a testable question.
st: Read an open demonstration's stated idea before touching only controls visitors may use.
Name one variable that could change in a safe repeat of the demonstration.
Predict a result and label it as a prediction, not a finding the display proved.
Choose an open Maymont path with a visible change in planting, grade or enclosure.
Record how the first space guides a walker into the next without touching plants or railings.
Draw a simple transition diagram and mark which parts are observed rather than assumed.

packs.title: Capitol to Church Hill
packs.promise: Walk Richmond's civic center, Shockoe streets and Church Hill with care.

q.s: Map how public grounds frame a state building.
st: Find two open approaches to Capitol Square without leaving public paths.
Choose one view of the Capitol and record the path, planting or grade that leads to it.
Draw a small approach map that distinguishes public access from any closed area.

q.s: Turn one exhibited source into a careful question.
st: Choose one currently open exhibition item and record its title or credit.
Write one detail the source actually supports, without treating a display as the whole story.
Ask one question that the item leaves open and identify what further source could help.

q.s: Compare two public street edges in Shockoe Slip.
st: From a safe public point, notice one paving or slope detail and one reused building edge.
Compare how each guides a person moving through the district.
Sketch a short route that avoids blocked, private or rough surfaces.
